slides.headline: Airlines Pay You Not to Fly
slides.subheadline: Extra reservations earn revenue—until too many passengers show.

items.label: Revenue opportunity
items.body: Extra reservations can fill seats no-shows leave empty.

items.label: Capacity shortfall
items.body: Too many arrivals turn extra bookings into displacement.

visualStyle.name: Swiss typographic collision
visualStyle.typography: Heavy grotesk headlines; restrained sans-serif captions.
visualStyle.treatment: Flat vector geometry, oversized type, no gradients.

slides.layoutTopology: Asymmetric masthead above a monumental central collision diagram.

svgBlueprint.construction: Draw a thick black reservation ribbon entering a narrow aircraft-door outline. Fold the overflow into a red return arrow. Keep the aircraft door abstract; depict no numerical seat capacity.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Wrap the headline after 'You'. Anchor the two items beneath opposite ends of the diagram.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: Black forward motion represents additional bookings; the red return represents displacement when attendance exceeds capacity.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: Reservations can exceed available seats when more passengers arrive than forecast.

slides.headline: Displacement Has Two Ledgers

visualStyle.name: Statistical ledger
visualStyle.typography: Tabular numerals with small uppercase ledger labels.
visualStyle.treatment: Hairline rules and generous white space.

slides.layoutTopology: Two vertically stacked, full-width numerical registers.

svgBlueprint.construction: Set 69,566 in black across the upper register and 5,542 in red across the lower register. Separate them with a single black rule. Place a pale-gray rectangular field behind the lower register.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Use each item's label above its numerical register. The large numeral replaces repetition of the corresponding item body.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: Equal register dimensions distinguish reporting categories without implying equal counts.
svgBlueprint.scope: Reporting marketing carriers, including branded codeshare partners where applicable.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: These counts describe denied-boarding outcomes, not overbooking frequency or profit.

slides.headline: Compare Exposure, Not Raw Counts

visualStyle.name: Precision comparison
visualStyle.typography: Compact carrier labels; oversized tabular endpoint values.
visualStyle.treatment: Unembellished bars on a common zero baseline.

slides.layoutTopology: Left-aligned carrier labels above two horizontal comparison tracks.

svgBlueprint.construction: Draw two horizontal bars beginning at x=72. Map bar length linearly to the published rates: Frontier width=780; American width=780×0.64÷1.66. Use red for Frontier and black for American.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Place carrier names above their bars and exact published rates below their endpoints. Keep labels outside the bars.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: Bar length encodes involuntary denied-boardings per 10,000 enplaned passengers. Use neither raw counts nor a truncated baseline.
svgBlueprint.scope: Reporting marketing carriers, including branded codeshare partners where applicable.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: Frontier's published rate was 1.66; American Airlines Network's was 0.64.

slides.headline: Forecast First. Resolve at Boarding.
slides.subheadline: A booking forecast becomes a capacity decision.

items.label: Before departure
items.body: Sell reservations; forecast no-shows; accept extra bookings.

items.label: At boarding
items.body: Check attendance; seek volunteers; apply fair priorities.

visualStyle.name: Operational schematic
visualStyle.typography: Technical sans-serif labels with emphatic phase headings.
visualStyle.treatment: Orthogonal connectors and two large, uncluttered process chambers.

slides.layoutTopology: Vertical two-stage pipeline with a narrow attendance checkpoint.

svgBlueprint.construction: Draw an upper black-outline chamber and a lower pale-gray chamber. Connect them with one downward arrow crossing a red horizontal threshold. Place one item inside each chamber; do not subdivide them into additional cards.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Set each phase label prominently, with its body wrapped into short sequential lines.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: The upper chamber represents uncertain attendance. The lower chamber represents resolving actual attendance against available seats.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: When attendance exceeds seats, solicit volunteers first. If insufficient, apply fair boarding priorities and compensate eligible involuntarily displaced passengers.

slides.headline: Zero Bumping Can Hide Displacement

items.label: Volunteer terms
items.body: No offer ceiling; voucher restrictions must be disclosed.

visualStyle.name: Negative-space reveal
visualStyle.typography: Monumental outline numeral paired with a solid red counterfigure.
visualStyle.treatment: A visual contradiction built from two exact reported values.

slides.layoutTopology: Oversized outlined zero on the left; red numerical reveal on the right.

svgBlueprint.construction: Render a giant outlined 0 in black. Align 23,699 in red beside it, not inside it. Give both values explicit denied-boarding category labels. Add a black bracket beneath the pair leading to the volunteer-terms item.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Use the numerical pair to render the first item. Place the second item in a single full-width strip below the hero.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: The zero describes involuntary outcomes only. The red value reveals voluntary displacement excluded from that zero.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: Delta reported 23,699 voluntary and 0 involuntary denied-boardings. Volunteer offers have no regulatory maximum.

slides.headline: 400% Is Not Automatic
slides.subheadline: Eligible involuntary denials: planned arrival delay matters.

items.label: Domestic trigger
items.body: 2+ hours: at least min(400% × applicable fare, $2,150).

items.label: International trigger
items.body: 4+ hours: at least min(400% × applicable fare, $2,150).

slides.footnote: One-way fare; international departures from U.S. airports. No qualifying substitute also triggers this tier. Eligibility and exceptions apply; larger payments permitted.

visualStyle.name: Regulatory decision plate
visualStyle.typography: Heavy percentage headline, monospaced formulas, readable legal note.
visualStyle.treatment: Two precise rule-bound panels; red reserved for conditional thresholds.

slides.layoutTopology: Paired vertical jurisdiction panels beneath a shared conditional headline.

svgBlueprint.construction: Draw two equal outlined panels separated by a wide white gutter. Give each a red arrival-delay threshold and the compensation formula beneath it. Use stacked mathematical typography rather than shrinking either formula.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Place jurisdiction labels above the panels. Wrap the footnote below them at a readable size. Do not depict $2,150 as a guaranteed payment.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: These panels show only the higher compensation tier, not the complete payment schedule. Applicable fare means applicable one-way fare.
svgBlueprint.timingBasis: Compare substitute transportation's planned arrival, when arranged, with the original planned arrival.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: Subject to eligibility and exceptions, the higher tier requires at least the lesser of 400% of applicable one-way fare and $2,150. Domestic delay threshold: 2 hours or more. International departing a U.S. airport: 4 hours or more. No qualifying substitute transportation also triggers this tier.

slides.headline: Extra Revenue Must Survive Costs
slides.subheadline: Optimize retained revenue—not the number of extra tickets.

items.label: Net economics
items.body: Subtract compensation, transport and recovery costs.

items.label: Audit together
items.body: Forecasts, volunteer deals, rights and outcome reporting.

visualStyle.name: Architectural accounting gate
visualStyle.typography: Decisive grotesk headline with spare accounting labels.
visualStyle.treatment: One strong geometric gate; no invented profit figure.

slides.layoutTopology: Central subtraction gate above a two-column editorial conclusion.

svgBlueprint.construction: Draw a broad black ribbon passing through a red rectangular gate. Continue a narrower black ribbon beyond it. Make all widths explicitly schematic, without ticks, percentages or numerical labels.
svgBlueprint.textPlacement: Place the net-economics item beneath the incoming ribbon and the audit item beneath the gate. Leave the outgoing ribbon unnumbered.
svgBlueprint.semanticMapping: The gate represents displacement and recovery costs deducted from incremental revenue. It does not assert a measured profit or a guaranteed positive return.
svgBlueprint.accessibility: Overbooking is explicitly regulated, not an unregulated loophole. Audit classification: accepting compensation after involuntary denial does not make the passenger a volunteer.
